subject: Renewal handoff: cohort co-term + staged ramp / billing cutover
messages:
From: Jules Park <jules.park@acmehealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — co-terming subsidiaries / multi-year options

Hi Mina,

Quick note from procurement here — our current Redwood agreement ends 2028-08-15 and we
want to consolidate a handful of teams under a single renewal (three legal entities).
We have a few asks up front:
- Can you outline multi-year pricing options (2yr vs 3yr) with stair-step/onramp credits?
- We want to co-term all subsidiaries to 2029-08-15 if possible (one invoice cadence).
- Procurement asks whether an auto-renew opt-out window can be included (we need a 45-day opt-out).

Also, our finance team wants a short billing cutover plan if we change cadence.
Can we get a quick options doc and a forecast to share with stakeholders?

Thanks,
Jules
Jules Park
Director, Cloud Procurement
Acme Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal conversation — co-terming subsidiaries / multi-year options

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Key constraints: 3 legal entities, need co-term to 2029-08-15, and a 45-day auto-renew opt-out.
I've sketched 3 options in attached Draft_Amendment_v1.docx and included a usage forecast (Usage_Forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx) they shared as a baseline. High-level thoughts below:

Option A — 24-month locked term, 10% uplift discount vs current list, staged ramp (year 1 = 60% committed, year 2 = 100%). Billing stays quarterly but invoice consolidated across entities.
Option B — 36-month with deeper discount (15%), conversion credit front-loaded in Q1 to help onboarding; billing annual in advance for consolidated entity.
Option C — 12 + 12 (auto-renew unless opt-out) with canary rollback and usage true-up every 6 months.

Trade-offs: co-terming simplifies ops but requires aligned legal signatures and PO timing. Procurement wants to avoid surprise auto-renew; we should offer a 45-day written opt-out window in the amendment.

Ask: Karthik — can you confirm feasibility of the staged ramp + canary fallback in our Dedicated pools?
Kimberly — please confirm pricing table and whether Finance is comfortable with consolidated invoicing cadence (quarterly vs annual).
Marissa — can you review the proposed SOW language around billing cutover (we may need an implementation window)?

I'll coordinate a call with Acme for next week if we have internal alignment.

Attachments: Draft_Amendment_v1.docx; Usage_Forecast_Q3-Q4.xlsx

Best,
Mina
Senior AE, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal conversation — co-terming subsidiaries / multi-year options

Mina — thanks for the summary. Quick feasibility notes from infra/ops:

- Staged ramp: we can implement a stair-step commit profile (60% -> 80% -> 100% over the first 12 months) with automatic throttling triggers if observed usage exceeds committed thresholds. That maps to our existing burst+reserve model.
- Canary fallback: we can route a percentage of traffic to the existing model endpoint for first 30 days post-cut, then flip once stability metrics are green.
- Co-terming multiple legal entities is operationally straightforward but requires: single billing owner (PO/AP contact), consolidated HUBSPOT deal line (suggest HS-4291-AH), and legal signature visibility across subsidiaries.

Procurement timeline question: if they want co-term by 2029-08-15, we should lock commercial terms by 2028-06-15 to allow redlines and internal legal review.

I'll draft an ops checklist and a short failure-mode runbook. Sending my suggested redline bullets inline to the attached draft.

Karthik
Head of Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Mina / Karthik — pricing & billing notes from Finance side:

- Pricing: for Option A (24m staged ramp) propose an overall blended rate that starts at current list * 0.90 for Yr1 and steps to current list * 0.95 Yr2 (effectively ~12% average discount across term). For Option B (36m) propose 15% off list with a 20% conversion credit applied in Q1.
- Billing cadence: Acme prefers consolidated invoices. We can support consolidated quarterly invoices across legal entities if Acme provides a primary invoice recipient and PO mapping per entity. If they choose annual prepay we need PO and treasury clearance 30 days before term start.
- Auto-renew opt-out: 45-day written window is fine. Legal will want explicit language about what constitutes 'notice' (email to commercial@redwood.com or DocuSign opt-out).

I've attached a pricing table and a high-level billing cutover timeline for review. If we go with consolidated quarterly invoicing we should schedule the billing cutover for the start of a quarter; otherwise prorates will be messy.

Attachments: Pricing_Table_v3.csv; Billing_Cutover_Timeline.pdf

Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jules — internal alignment complete enough to propose a path forward. Summary and next steps below:

Chosen path (recommended): Option A variant — 24-month term with staged ramp (60% commit -> 100% at month 12), consolidated quarterly invoicing across entities, 45-day written auto-renew opt-out. We add a 30-day canary period for cutover with automated fallback.

Deliverables we'll send today:
- Updated amendment (Draft_Amendment_v3.docx) with explicit opt-out language and co-term mechanics.
- Usage forecast workbook (we'll merge your numbers with our projection).
- Ops checklist + failure-mode runbook for the canary cutover (link included).

Action items / timeline:
1) Internal sign-off: Redwood legal & finance to turn around redlines by 2028-06-05.
2) Commercial lock: finalize commercial terms by 2028-06-15 (to meet Acme's timeline).
3) Procurement / PO: Acme to provide PO mapping and primary invoice recipient by 2028-06-20.
4) Implementation: schedule canary cutover for the first business week of August; target full co-term activation 2028-08-15.

Doc links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-ACME-renewal (amendments and timelines). DocuSign link will be generated after redlines.

Please review Draft_Amendment_v3.docx attached and confirm if you want us to move forward with the 24-month staged path. If you want to discuss other discount levers, happy to hop on a 30-min call.

Best,
